problems.name: HumanEval_108_count_nums
problems.code:
def count_nums(arr)
 arr.count do |n|
 if n >= 0
 n.to_s.chars.map(&:to_i).sum > 0
 else
 abs = n.abs
 sum = abs.to_s.chars.map(&:to_i).sum
 first = abs.to_s[0].to_i
 (sum - 2 * first) > 0
 end
 end
end

  def test_count_nums
    candidate = method(:count_nums)
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call([]))
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call([-1, -2, 0]))
    assert_equal(6, candidate.call([1, 1, 2, -2, 3, 4, 5]))
    assert_equal(5, candidate.call([1, 6, 9, -6, 0, 1, 5]))
    assert_equal(4, candidate.call([1, 100, 98, -7, 1, -1]))
    assert_equal(5, candidate.call([12, 23, 34, -45, -56, 0]))
    assert_equal(1, candidate.call([0, 1]))
    assert_equal(1, candidate.call([1]))
  end
end

def minPath(grid, k)
 n = grid.length
 # find cell with value 1
 start = nil
 grid.each_with_index do |row, i|
 row.each_with_index do |val, j|
 if val == 1
 start = [i, j]
 break
 end
 end
 break if start
 end
 # if k == 1, return [1]
 path = [1]
 i, j = start
 (k-1).times do
 neighbors = []
 # up
 if i > 0
 neighbors << [i-1, j, grid[i-1][j]]
 end
 # down
 if i < n-1
 neighbors << [i+1, j, grid[i+1][j]]
 end
 # left
 if j > 0
 neighbors << [i, j-1, grid[i][j-1]]
 end
 # right
 if j < n-1
 neighbors << [i, j+1, grid[i][j+1]]
 end
 best = neighbors.min_by { |_,_, val| val }
 path << best[2]
 i, j = best[0], best[1]
 end
 path
end
